conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: BullTrendBar
candidates.quote: the move had about four consecutive bull trend bars or two or three large bull trend bars
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar is a bull trend bar — it closed up and its body is at least a fraction of its high-low range.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

notes: Brooks gives no number; 0.6 reads 'body is most of the range'. Used by T10-05, T10-06, T10-12, T10-13, T10-16, T10-18.

candidates.name: BullReversalBar
candidates.quote: Traders could have gone long on bar 9 after the bar 8 reversal bar
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bull reversal bar — it traded below the prior bar's low, closed up, and closed in the upper part of its range (tail at the bottom).
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < low[1] && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - low[0]) >= closePosFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the reversal bar's high (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic

notes: The lower-low term is the 'reversal' part; drop it for a plain 'bull bar with a bottom tail'.

candidates.name: SecondReversalSignal
candidates.quote: It is better to wait for an entry, not take it, wait for the trend to resume for a bar or two, and then enter on the market's second attempt to reverse.
candidates.description: The current bar is a bull reversal bar AND there was an earlier bull reversal bar within the last N bars with at least one non-signal bar between them (the trend resumed). Only the second attempt is taken.
candidates.pseudocode: isBullReversalBar(0) && !isBullReversalBar(1) && countTrue(isBullReversalBar(i) for i in 2..maxBarsBetween) >= 1
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the second signal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: window scan of a derived bar classification rather than a fixed offset

notes: Brooks's second entry also implies the first entry did not run to a scalper's profit; T10-04 and T12-01 capture the 'first entry failed' side.
A stricter form requires low[0] to be within tolerance of the first signal bar's low (a micro double bottom, T10-08).

candidates.name: SecondEntryNotAtBetterPrice
candidates.quote: If the second entry is letting you in at a better price than the first, be suspicious that it might be a trap. Most good second entries are at the same price or worse.
candidates.description: Gate on T10-03: the second signal bar's entry price (its high) is at or above the first signal bar's high. A second entry offered at a lower price is skipped ('good fill, bad trade').
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] >= high[firstSignalBarIndex] - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (filter on a stop-entry price)

complexity.reason: must locate the first signal bar found by T10-03 and compare against its high

notes: Figure 10.1 bar 10 is the counter-example: one tick better than bar 9, and it failed.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveTrendBarsBlockCountertrend
candidates.quote: Bar 1 followed five bull trend bars, which is too much upward momentum to be shorting the first attempt down.
candidates.description: Countertrend gate, written for a LONG (countertrend) entry: fewer than N of the last N bars were bear trend bars. Equivalently, do not buy the first reversal after N or more consecutive bear trend bars.
candidates.pseudocode: countTrue(isBearTrendBar(i) for i in 1..minConsecutive) < minConsecutive
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: window count of a single-bar classification

notes: Brooks uses four (p207), five (p209 bar 1), and four (p209 bar 5; p210 'high 2 after four bear trend bars should not be bought'). This is ConsecutiveUpBars negated with the trend-bar body test added.
Brooks's remedy is to wait for the second entry (T10-03), not to skip the trade altogether.

candidates.name: LargeTrendBarsBlockCountertrend
candidates.quote: the move had about four consecutive bull trend bars or two or three large bull trend bars, there is too much momentum for you to be placing an order in the opposite direction
candidates.description: Countertrend gate for a LONG entry: fewer than K of the last N bars were bear trend bars with range above a multiple of ATR.
candidates.pseudocode: countTrue(isBearTrendBar(i) && (high[i] - low[i]) > largeBarAtrMult * atr(atrLength) for i in 1..lookback) < maxLargeBars
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: ATR plus a window count

notes: 'Large' is not quantified; 1.5x ATR is a placeholder for the grid.

candidates.name: CountertrendNeedsPriorPush
candidates.quote: Before taking a countertrend trade, it is always better to see some evidence in the preceding several bars that the bulls were able to move more than just a couple of ticks above the prior bar.
candidates.description: Gate for a countertrend LONG: within the last N bars, at least one bar's high exceeded the previous bar's high by more than K ticks.
candidates.pseudocode: countTrue((high[i] - high[i+1]) > minPushTicks * tickSize for i in 1..lookback) >= 1
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: window scan of adjacent-bar high differences

notes: Figure 10.1: the tight bear channel from bar 8 had no such push, so the bar 10 long was suspect.

candidates.name: MicroDoubleBottom
candidates.quote: Bar 8 was a micro double bottom (a buy setup) since the market went down on bar 8 and it also went down two bars earlier (bear bar).
candidates.description: Two lows within a small tolerance of each other separated by one bar, the second closing up: |low[0] - low[2]| within K ticks, low[1] above both, and close[0] > open[0]. Brooks: most bottoms are some form of micro double bottom (and tops a micro double top).
candidates.pseudocode: abs(low[0] - low[2]) <= toleranceTicks * tickSize && low[1] > min(low[0], low[2]) && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the second bar's high (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: fixed-offset three-bar comparison

notes: Brooks's examples use a 1-bar gap (bar 8 and two bars earlier; bar 18 and the bar before bar 17). A parameter gapBars could generalize the [2] offset.
Tolerance should scale with tick size or ATR for cross-symbol use.

candidates.name: NoBullCloseForNBarsWaitForSecond
candidates.quote: Bar 3 was a first entry long on a new low of the day, but after six bars without a bullish close it makes more sense to wait for a second long entry
candidates.description: Gate for a first-entry LONG: at least one of the last N bars closed above its open. When none did, the first long signal is skipped (only a second entry, T10-03, is allowed).
candidates.pseudocode: countTrue(close[i] > open[i] for i in 1..lookback) >= 1
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: window count of up-closes

notes: Equivalent to NOT ConsecutiveUpBars(6) on the short side.

candidates.name: HigherLowsSeriesBlocksShort
candidates.quote: Bar 10 followed six bars with higher lows and only two bars with small bear bodies, indicating too much bullish strength for a short.
candidates.description: Gate for a countertrend LONG (mirror of Brooks's short example): fewer than M of the last N bars made a lower high than the bar before it. A run of lower highs means too much bearish strength to buy the first reversal.
candidates.pseudocode: countTrue(high[i] < high[i+1] for i in 1..lookback) < maxLowerHighs
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: window count of adjacent-bar comparisons

notes: The 'only two small bear bodies' clause is a second gate: count of bear bars in the window <= K (covered by T10-09's family).

candidates.name: DojiBar
candidates.quote: Bar 11 was a doji reversal bar after a big bull trend bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the bar's body is at most a small fraction of its range.
candidates.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiBodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

candidates.name: DojiAfterBigTrendBarReversal
candidates.quote: Bar 11 was a doji reversal bar after a big bull trend bar.
candidates.description: LONG form (mirror of the book's short): the previous bar was a big bear trend bar (range above K x ATR) and the current bar is a doji — a possible sell climax and reversal. Enter long at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: isBearTrendBar(1) && (high[1] - low[1]) > bigBarAtrMult * atr(atrLength) && isDoji(0)
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the doji's low (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: ATR plus fixed-offset bar tests

notes: Brooks treats this as a scalp toward the moving average (T10-15) rather than a swing.

candidates.name: BuyClimaxBigBarAfterRun
candidates.quote: A big bull trend bar after five to 10 bar bull trend bars is a buy climax and is likely to be followed by about 10 or more sideways to down bars before the bulls return.
candidates.description: Exit the long when the current bar is a bull trend bar with range above K x ATR and at least M of the last N bars were bull trend bars (buy climax).
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && isBullTrendBar(0) && (high[0] - low[0]) > bigBarAtrMult * atr(atrLength) && countTrue(isBullTrendBar(i) for i in 1..lookback) >= minTrendBars
candidates.book_order_type: take profits at the market / on the close

complexity.reason: ATR plus a window count; no persistent state

notes: Companion Entry filter is T10-14.

candidates.name: NoLongsAfterBuyClimaxForNBars
candidates.quote: is likely to be followed by about 10 or more sideways to down bars before the bulls return
candidates.description: Gate on LONG entries: no buy climax (T10-13's condition) occurred within the last P bars.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSince(buyClimaxCondition) > blockBars
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: a bars-since counter that persists across bars

candidates.name: ScalpExitAtEmaTest
candidates.quote: Some bear scalpers shorted there, expecting at least a test down to the moving average.
candidates.description: Exit the long (mirror of the book's short scalp) once the bar's high reaches the N-bar EMA — the moving average is the minimum target of a countertrend scalp.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && high[0] >= xaverage(close, emaLength)
candidates.book_order_type: limit at the moving average

complexity.reason: needs an EMA

notes: Written for a long entered below the EMA; if entered above it the exit fires immediately — gate on entry price below the EMA at entry if needed.

candidates.name: ThreeConsecutiveSellClimaxesBuy
candidates.quote: All three bear spikes in this channel down from that low 4 short constitute consecutive sell climaxes, and once there are three, the odds of at least a two-legged rally are high.
candidates.description: Three separate bear spikes (each a run of at least S consecutive bear trend bars, separated by at least one non-bear-trend bar) within the last N bars, followed by a bull reversal bar: buy.
candidates.pseudocode: countSpikes(isBearTrendBar, minSpikeBars, lookback) >= 3 && isBullReversalBar(0)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: counting distinct runs (spikes) inside a variable window is pattern recognition, not a fixed-offset test

notes: The spikes in the example were 4, 4 and 2 bars long; minSpikeBars=2 matches.
Target: 'at least a two-legged rally' — see T14-15 for leg-count exits.

candidates.name: IiPattern
candidates.quote: The bar 7 ii was a possible final flag.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: two consecutive inside bars (bar[0] inside bar[1], bar[1] inside bar[2]).
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1] && high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (pattern primitive; Brooks enters on a stop beyond the ii in either direction)

complexity.reason: fixed-offset three-bar comparison

notes: Equals InsideBar(0) AND InsideBar(1) with <= instead of strict.

candidates.name: IiFinalFlagAfterBearRunBuy
candidates.quote: The bar 7 ii was a possible final flag.
candidates.description: An ii pattern forming after a bear run (at least M bear trend bars in the last N bars) is a possible final flag; buy when the bar after the ii closes above the ii's high.
candidates.pseudocode: isIi(1) && countTrue(isBearTrendBar(i) for i in 3..lookback) >= minBearBars && close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the ii high (mechanized: close above it, then next bar open)

complexity.reason: window count plus fixed-offset tests

notes: 'Final flag' proper needs the flag to be the last pullback of a protracted trend — a research-grade context; this mechanization approximates it with a bear-bar count.

candidates.name: DipBelowPriorBarInStrongBullBuy
candidates.quote: it made more sense to look to buy a higher low or even on a limit order below the prior bar. With this much upward momentum, the market was very likely to at least test the high of the leg up.
candidates.description: In a strong bull context (a run of higher lows), buy when the current bar dips below the prior bar's low — the limit-order pullback buy — entering at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < low[1] && countTrue(low[i] > low[i+1] for i in 1..lookback) >= minHigherLows
candidates.book_order_type: limit order below the prior bar's low

complexity.reason: window count plus fixed-offset comparison

notes: A limit entry, not a stop entry; mechanizing at the next open gives up the fill inside the bar.

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutAtEma
candidates.quote: The market ... broke above the bear channel into yesterday's close, but the breakout failed at the moving average, setting up a short.
candidates.description: LONG form (mirror): in a bull context (close above the EMA for the last N bars) the bar dips through the EMA (low below it) but closes back above it — a failed breakout at the moving average. Buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < ema && close[0] > ema && countTrue(close[i] > ema[i] for i in 1..priorBars) >= priorBars where ema = xaverage(close, emaLength)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the signal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window of EMA relations

notes: Brooks's original is a bear-channel breakout above that failed at the EMA; the channel part is dropped here.

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutOfPriorDayLow
candidates.quote: Today the market broke out below yesterday's low, but the breakout failed on the reversal up on the fourth bar of the day.
candidates.description: Intraday: the bar's low breaks below the prior session's low but the bar closes back above it — a failed breakout. Buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < prevSessionLow && close[0] > prevSessionLow && barsIntoSession <= maxBarsIntoSession
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs a prior-session low tracked across a date change

notes: Brooks also frames it as a breakout pullback to a lower low after the first bar broke above a small bear channel.

candidates.name: FailedTestOfPriorSwingExtreme
candidates.quote: Traders should have shorted below the bar 6 double top because ... the market failed to break above a prior lower high. The trend of lower highs and lows was continuing.
candidates.description: LONG form (mirror): the bar's low comes within tolerance of the most recent swing low but does not break it, and the bar closes up — a double bottom / failed test of the prior extreme. Buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: abs(low[0] - lastSwingLow) <= toleranceAtr * atr(atrLength) && low[0] >= lastSwingLow && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the signal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs a confirmed swing-low pivot (lowest low with swingStrength higher lows on each side) located at variable distance

notes: A window approximation: lastSwingLow = lowest(low, N)[1] with the current bar excluded.

candidates.name: High2Setup
candidates.quote: Bar 5 was a high 2 but it followed four bear trend bars and therefore should not be bought.
candidates.description: Shared primitive (counting setup): within a pullback in a bull trend, a high 1 is the first bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high; after that fails to resume the trend and a further down-move occurs, the next bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high is the high 2. Buy above the high 2 signal bar. The low 4 is the second low 2 of a larger pullback.
candidates.pseudocode: state machine: reset count on a new trend high; count += 1 each time high[0] > high[1] after at least one bar with high <= prior high since the last count; signal when count == entryNumber && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the H2 signal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: leg counting inside a pullback with a reset on new trend extremes — cross-bar state and a pullback definition

notes: Brooks defines H1/H2/L1/L2 fully in book 2 (Ranges); this chapter uses them without definition.
Low 4 (p210) is entryNumber=4 on the short side.

candidates.name: TakeProfitAtPriorSwingHighTest
candidates.quote: It is also in the area of the final lower high of the bear trend, creating a potential double top bear flag ... they used the double top bear flag as an area to take profits.
candidates.description: Exit the long when the bar's high reaches within tolerance of the most recent prior swing high (the potential double top).
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && high[0] >= lastSwingHigh - toleranceAtr * atr(atrLength)
candidates.book_order_type: limit / take profit at the prior high

complexity.reason: needs a confirmed swing-high pivot at variable distance

notes: Window approximation: highest(high, N)[1] before the current leg.

rejected.quote: Traders looking for second entries are more aggressive and confident and will often enter on smaller time frame charts.
rejected.reason: needs a lower time frame than the bar series

rejected.quote: Most of the time, a good fill equals a bad trade (and a bad fill equals a good trade!).
rejected.reason: aphorism; the decidable part is captured by T10-04

rejected.quote: As discussed in book 3, most tops occur from some type of micro double top
rejected.reason: statistical claim, captured as T10-08 mirrored; no separate test

chapter_summary: Second entries: a second reversal attempt is more reliable than the first, should not come at a better price, and is mandatory after strong momentum (four-plus consecutive trend bars, two or three large trend bars, six bars without a bull close, six higher lows). Produced the second-entry family (T10-03/04), the momentum-blocks-countertrend filters (T10-05/06/07/09/10), primitives BullTrendBar, BullReversalBar, DojiBar, IiPattern, MicroDoubleBottom, and a set of chart-example setups (buy climax, three sell climaxes, failed breakout of yesterday's low, failed breakout at the EMA, H2). H2 is used here without a definition; book 2 will define it properly.
